done_when: When two rounds in a row leave the same failing test or finding, or the change grows past its size limit, Forge stops the item and prints a ready-to-ask question naming the item, what is stuck and what the worker tried, with the choices: switch this item to the other tool, keep the same tool for one more round, or narrow or split; the owner's choice is recorded and the next round follows it

findings.body: Raise: Not done. When a worker completes two rounds without changing product code, close reuses the blocking review and its `commit`; with passing tests, `tested_head` also stays unchanged. This equality check returns without counting the second round, so the same finding can be sent back indefinitely instead of producing the required question. The named finding proof uses a worker that commits a change.
findings.title: Not done: unchanged review findings can loop indefinitely

findings.body: Raise: Not done. This records a stuck-stop `narrow` or `split` choice, but the next `forge work` passes an owner-choice note only when `stop.by == "owner"` and `worker_round` matches (worker.py:156-163). A stuck stop sets neither field, and `stuck_round` removes that stop before building the brief. The worker therefore receives no instruction to narrow or split. The named test checks only that another worker ran.
findings.title: Not done: narrow and split choices do not reach the next worker

findings.body: Raise: Not done. A story part can grow past its line limit during the round after the owner resolves an earlier review-loop stop. That recorded stop still exists, so `if not stop` is false and close returns the old split-or-allow-large refusal instead of the required ready-to-ask question about the oversized change. The size proof starts with no earlier stop.
findings.title: Not done: an earlier stop suppresses the size-limit question

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The question gets “The worker tried” only from commit subjects and prints “no new commits” when that list is empty. A worker can attempt a fix, leave the failure in place, and finish without a code commit; the owner then sees no account of the attempt. The named question proof uses a worker that commits “Worker round.”
findings.title: Not done: the question omits what a worker without commits tried

findings.body: Raise: Functional. The stop check runs after `machine.agent_slot` admission at worker.py:124-125. As machine.py:175-203 shows, another active worker and load of at least 1.5 per core can keep admission waiting. On a normally busy machine, an item already due to stop remains queued without its ready-to-ask question until a worker slot opens.
findings.title: Not done: a stuck item waits for a worker slot before asking the owner

why: When a worker can't fix a problem or keeps making the change bigger, Forge sends it back round after round and nobody is told
